question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡y\,i+\frac{x}{1+{y}^{2}}\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x={t}^{2}+1$ and $y=t$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{1+{t}^{2}}\,j \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\,i+j)\cdot (2t\,i+j) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡t\cdot 2t+1\cdot 1 \\  & =2t\operatorname{arctan}⁡t+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =2(1)\operatorname{arctan}⁡1+1 \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}+1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{\pi +2}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
